title: The Value 'nil'
referenceMarkdown:
`nil` represents the absence of any value in Lua. Declaring a variable without assigning a value automatically sets it to `nil`:

`local emptyVariable`
`print(emptyVariable)  -- nil`

Use `local` to declare variables scoped to the current block. `nil` is distinct from `0`, `""`, or `false` — it means no value has been assigned.
challengeMarkdown: Create a variable called `playerStatus` without assigning any value to it. Then print this variable to see what Lua assigns by default.
hints: Use the local keyword, followed by just the variable name — no equals sign.
print() will show you exactly what value an unassigned variable holds.
